lines.text: Your headphones fight noise... with more noise. They make a second sound, the exact opposite of the first, and the two cancel out. Silence, made of sound. Let's slow it down and watch it happen.
Sound is a push through the air. A speaker shoves the air, squeezing it together, then pulls back, stretching it apart. Squeeze, stretch, squeeze, stretch. A wave, travelling to your ear.
Your eardrum rides those waves, in and out. Big waves sound loud. Fast waves sound high. And a plane engine makes slow, heavy waves. A low, endless hum.
In nineteen seventy eight, an engineer named Amar Bose sat on a long flight, wearing airline headphones. The engine hum drowned out his music. So he started sketching a fix, right there on the plane.
The idea itself is even older, from the nineteen thirties. Add a squeeze to a stretch, and you get... nothing. Lay a wave on top of its mirror image, and the air doesn't move at all.
So let's cut a pair open. A soft cushion seals around your ear. A speaker for your music. And tiny microphones. One listening outside, one listening inside.
The outside microphone hears the hum coming. It turns it into an electrical signal, and sends it to a chip.
The chip flips it. Every squeeze becomes a stretch. Every stretch becomes a squeeze. Anti noise.
The speaker plays your music, plus that anti noise, at the very moment the real hum arrives.
Squeeze meets stretch. Stretch meets squeeze. The two waves cancel, and the hum fades away. Your music stays.
It has to be fast. The chip works thousands of times a second, and the inside microphone keeps checking what's left over, and corrects it.
It works best on steady, low sounds. Engines, trains, the hum of a fan. Sudden, sharp sounds, like a clap or a voice, change too fast. So the cushion has to block those.
And the same microphones can do the opposite. Transparency mode passes the outside world into your ears, so you can still hear the announcement.
Noise cancelling stops the hum before it reaches you. Orbi Transfer protects your file before it even leaves. It's locked on your phone first.
It reaches the other phone in about a second. No login, no app. And after thirty minutes, it burns.
Orbi Transfer dot com. Silence, made of sound.
